So we need to search for config.py recursively. Use find tool. Then we need to display the last line of the file. Use tail. But we need to get the file name. The find tool returns a list of file names? Let\'s check find signature: find(path?: string, name?: string). It returns? Not specified but likely returns a list of matching file names. We can call find with name="config.py". Then we need to tail the first file. Use tail(file_name=first_file). That will show last 10 lines by default. But we want just the last line. tail has lines optional. We can set lines=1. So tail(file_name=first_file, lines=1). That should output the last line.\n\nWe need to call find first. Then tail. Let\'s do that.')
